what: States that the go build binary is named after the folder; Go actually names it after the last element of the module path, which only happens to match the folder here.
evidence: Page: "The binary is named after the folder: hello." A re-run with Go 1.27.3 in a scratch copy: in folder hello/, `go mod init example/zzz && go build` wrote a binary named `zzz`; in folder proj/, `go mod init example/hello && go build` wrote `hello`. cmd/go doc: build names the executable after the last element of the package import path.
fix: "The binary is named after the last part of the module path, example/hello: hello." (The chat note in panel 16 and the Lab can stay as they are.)

what: The terminal sessions run hidden setup the footer does not disclose: Go is removed from PATH to stage 'command not found', and go build runs after a silent go mod init in a freshly rebuilt folder. The footer also calls the sessions 'run one after another', but each one is a separate, rebuilt run.
evidence: /home/you/go-ch1/s_nogo.cmd shown as `go version`, really runs `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ... bash -i -c 'go version'`. s_build.cmd shown as `go build`, really runs `mkdir -p $D && cp s_build.go $D/main.go && cd $D && rm -f go.mod hello && go mod init example/hello 2>/dev/null && go build`. s_mkdir.cmd's `mkdir hello` first runs `rmdir hello`. Footer: "The terminal sessions ... are real commands run one after another through the capture tool's command list, in a scratch folder with no go.mod above it". By contrast, the ch2 footer does disclose its "fresh scratch module made by go mod init".
fix: Add to the footer: "Panel 14 ran with Go left off PATH (env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin) to show a machine without Go. Each session starts in a freshly made folder: panel 22's folder was rebuilt with main.go and a silent go mod init before go build." Replace "one after another" with "each in its own fresh folder". Optionally move these sessions to `session: true`.

what: The detective checklist says a bare file.go with no # header means go vet, and panel 12 says vet's lines have no header and no ./. Panel 21 then shows go vet output with two # headers and ./main.go, and panel 11 shows gofmt (not vet) printing a bare main.go:6:21.
evidence: P22: "A # header and ./file.go means the Compiler. A bare file.go with no header means go vet." P12: "Vet's lines have no # header and no ./." P21 terminal (s_vetsyntax.go, captured): "# example/sums\n# [example/sums]\nvet: ./main.go:6:21: missing ',' in argument list". P11 (s_fmtbroken.go): "main.go:6:21: missing ',' in argument list" from gofmt -l.
fix: P12: "For a suspicious-code finding, vet prints no # header and no ./." P22 item 1: "A line starting with vet: or a bare main.go after go vet means vet. A # header plus ./file.go after go build or go run means the Compiler. A bare file name after gofmt means Tidy."
